elements.evidence: Revised 12.4 reads: "Customer is not subject to any non-solicitation, no-hire, or similar restriction with respect to Vendor personnel." The prior one-sided 24-month solicit/hire/employ bar covering "any Vendor employee" is gone, and the confirmation is unconditional and aligned with 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no no-hire commitment.

No non-solicitation covenant survives in either direction; the redline deletes the covenant outright rather than rendering it mutual, so the fallback structure (a mutual, involvement-limited non-solicit) is not built. This is not a defect given the preferred level is fully met, but the fallback level is therefore incomplete.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no restriction of any kind on Customer as to Vendor personnel, there is no covenant reaching non-involved personnel.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the 24-month tail ("during the term or for twenty-four months afterward") is removed and no duration remains to exceed 12 months.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the negating language "regardless of how the employee applies" is deleted and no covenant remains that could capture responses to general advertising; 12.3 independently preserves hiring "any person who responds to general recruitment".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no solicitation covenant remains, so unsolicited approaches are unrestricted.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The express no-hire ("solicit, hire, or employ") is removed and replaced with a confirmation that Customer is subject to no "non-solicitation, no-hire, or similar restriction," curing the walk-away no-hire.

reasons: The preferred checklist is a single element and the rendered 12.4 satisfies it unconditionally: Customer bears no non-solicitation, no-hire, or similar restriction. Position-complete at the preferred level.

Minimality holds: only Section 12.4 is touched, the offending covenant is swapped for a concise one-sentence confirmation, and nothing else is deleted, duplicated, or added (no survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or reciprocal obligations on Vendor). Section 12.3, which is favourable to Customer, is retained verbatim.

A concise affirmative confirmation rather than bare deletion is acceptable here because it also removes the internal conflict with 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made "no ... no-hire commitment"; it adds no operative requirement outside the checklist.

Intent preserved: no undefined terms, dangling cross-references, or contradictory retained sentences; timing, remedies, and other commercial mechanics in Article 12 are unaffected, and no new obligation is imposed on Vendor.

Fallback level is intentionally not built (no mutual, involvement-limited, 12-month covenant with carve-outs), which is correct given the preferred level is complete; the margin comment properly reserves that fallback as a negotiating concession.
Severity raised to high: the original 12.4 was walk-away on three independent grounds under this rule (express no-hire, 24-month tail, all Vendor employees) and contradicted Section 12.3.
